'''Cabiria Andreian Cazacu''' (February 19, 1928 – May 22, 2018) was a [[Romania]]n mathematician known for her work in [[complex analysis]]. She held the chair in mathematical analysis at the [[University of Bucharest]] from 1973 to 1975, and was dean of the faculty of mathematics at the University of Bucharest from 1976 to 1984.{{r|cristea}}

==Life==
Andreian Cazacu was born on February 19, 1928, in [[Iași]], the daughter of mathematics teacher Ioan T. Ardeleanu.<ref>{{cite book | first=George | last=Șt Andonie | title=Istoria matematicii în România | trans-title=A History of Mathematics in Romania | location=Bucharest | publisher=Editura Ştiinţ 1967 | page=330 | oclc=834168444 | language=RO}}</ref> Towards the end of [[World War II]], her family became refugees in [[Bucharest]], where she completed her high school studies in 1945.{{r|cristea}} She then enrolled in the Faculty of Mathematics at the University of Bucharest, graduating with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in 1949;  her undergraduate thesis, on ''Generalized nilpotent groups'', was written under the guidance of [[Ion Barbu|Dan Barbilian]].{{r|obit}}{{r|Ornea}} She then continued at the university, first as a teaching assistant and then as a lecturer starting in 1950.{{r|cristea}} She became a student of [[Simion Stoilow]], completing a doctorate in 1955 under his supervision, with the dissertation ''Normally exhaustible [[Riemann surface]]s''.{{r|mgp}} After being named associate professor in 1955, she completed a [[habilitation]] in 1967, with the habilitation thesis ''Classes of Riemann coverings'', and was promoted to full professor in 1968.{{r|cristea}}

From 1951 to 1969 Andreian Cazacu held a research position at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]], where she was a leading participant in Stoilow's seminar on complex analysis.{{r|cristea}} She held visiting positions at the [[Free University of Berlin]], [[Université libre de Bruxelles]], the [[University of Helsinki]], the [[University of Łódź]], and [[Université de Moncton]].{{r|obit}}

Between 1976 and 2010 she supervised the Ph.D. theses of 15 students.<ref name=mgp/> Andreian Cazacu was one of the main organizers of eleven editions of the Romanian-Finnish Seminar on complex analysis and potential theory, founded by [[Rolf Nevanlinna]] and Stoilow; the proceedings of four of these seminars, for which she was an editor, appeared in the [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] [[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] series as four separate volumes.{{r|cristea-bis}}

She died on May 22, 2018, in Bucharest{{r|obit}} and was buried at [[Ghencea Cemetery]].{{r|ssmr}}

==Publications==
Andreian Cazacu wrote "approximately 100 scientific papers and six books".{{r|cristea}} The books include:
*{{cite book|title=Probleme moderne de teoria funcțiilor|trans-title=Modern problems of the theory of functions|language=ro|first1=Cabiria|last1=Andreian Cazacu|first2=Corneliu|last2= Constantinescu|first3= Martin|last3=Jurchescu|publisher=Editura Academiei Republicii Populare Române|location=Bucharest|year=1965|mr=0200105|oclc=6014733}}
*{{cite book|title=Topologie, categorii, suprafețe riemanniene|trans-title=Topology, categories, Riemann surfaces|language=ro| first1=Cabiria|last1=Andreian Cazacu|first2= Aristide |last2=Deleanu|first3= Martin|last3=Jurchescu|publisher=Editura Academiei Republicii Populare Române| location=Bucharest| year=1966|mr=0215663|oclc=4666024}}
*{{cite book|title=Theorie der Funktionen mehrerer komplexer Veränderlicher|trans-title=Theory of functions of several complex variables|series=Lehrbücher und Monographien aus dem Gebiet der Exakten Wissenschaften, Mathematische Reihe| volume=51|language=de| first=Cabiria|last=Andreian Cazacu|publisher= [[Birkhäuser]]|location=Basel-Stuttgart|year= 1975|mr=0473209|oclc=2090281|isbn=3-7643-0770-6}}

==Recognition==
Andreian Cazacu won the [[Simion Stoilow Prize]] of the [[Romanian Academy]] in 1966. In 1998 the [[University of Craiova]] gave her an honorary doctorate. She was awarded in 2000 the [[National Order of Faithful Service]], Officer rank by [[President of Romania|President]] [[Ion Iliescu]],{{r|ord}} while in 2011 she was awarded the National Order of Faithful Service, Commander rank by President [[Traian Băsescu]].{{r|ord1}} She became an honorary member of the Romanian Academy in 2006. In 2010, the journal ''Complex Variables and Elliptic Equations'' published a special issue in honor of her 80th birthday.{{r|cristea}}
